statement: CAR T cells delivered into the ventricles or intrathecally produced rapid, radiographically dramatic regression of recurrent glioblastoma in a small number of patients; in most, the tumour progressed again within months.

context.intervention: intraventricular or intrathecal CAR T (IL13Ralpha2; bivalent EGFR/IL13Ralpha2; CARv3-TEAM-E)

measurement.endpoint: radiographic tumour response and its duration
measurement.effect: regression within days to weeks; durable in a minority

replication.note: Three groups (City of Hope; Penn; Mass General), three different constructs, the same pattern of rapid response and limited durability.

drift: 'CAR T shrinks brain tumours' is accurate and is not the same as 'CAR T treats glioblastoma'. Seven patients across three reports, and the tumours came back in most of them.

provenance.method: manual reasoning from the cited sources' abstracts (Crossref/Europe PMC), checked 2026-09-14; no source opened at figure level
